scope: Worker recovery after an actual isolated SQLAlchemy flush/commit failure; not external integration acceptance

defect.before: Both video and upload error handlers read expired task.id before rollback, causing PendingRollbackError and escaping the failure boundary.

change: Use the queue message task_id, already captured before ORM work, when logging the original exception. Rollback, refresh and terminal-state behavior remain unchanged.

targeted_tests.video: Real NOT NULL violation on task.queue; original queue restored and task FAILED; next valid task succeeds.
targeted_tests.upload: Real NOT NULL violation from the non-network transfer fixture; adapter closed, task FAILED, duplicate execution suppressed and next valid task succeeds; source fixture bytes preserved.

deployment.status: installed and bounded native frame recovery verified
deployment.log_check: 225 lines from 16:17:27 through 16:17:48; no ERROR, CRITICAL or Traceback markers
deployment.rollback: Restore only video.py and uploader.py from a4c84df5 or the verified backup, restart capture and verify both cameras; no database or configuration restore.

limitations: No malformed task or failed database write injected into production.
A persistently unavailable database cannot be made writable by rollback; this test covers a recoverable transaction failure.
No external upload destination or 24-hour observation covered.
